title: Verification on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

blocks.text: EquiLane verifies that Intel Intrinsics have been ported correctly to other CPUs. Ubuntu 26.04 LTS in Docker provides the shared reference environment. The output of the Intel C implementation for the same input is the reference used to check whether OpenPOWER, ARM64 NEON, and RISC-V64 RVV satisfy each case contract. Architectures that differ from the host run through an emulator.

The architecture-specific repositories in the table are builds of the official Ubuntu image.
The Dockerfile uses the same official multi-architecture image and selects its target with `--platform`.
The base image is pinned to the 26.04 manifest digest.

Docker Engine and Buildx are required. Docker Desktop includes emulation for building and running other architectures.
The available targets depend on the Docker installation; check emulator support if execution fails.

On Linux, register binfmt once on the Docker host if needed.
This administrative command updates the host binfmt configuration.
docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install amd64,arm64,ppc64le,riscv64

See the [Docker multi-platform guide](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/multi-platform/) for details.
The script does not run this administrative command automatically.
The CPU baseline required by Ubuntu and the compilation target of the wrappers are configured separately.

items: Ubuntu 26.04 on OpenPOWER requires POWER9 or later. QEMU selects `power9`, while the wrappers are built for POWER8.

Ubuntu 26.04 on RISC-V requires RVA23. Use the `rva23s64` CPU in QEMU 10.1 or later.
The wrappers are built with `-march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -mrvv-vector-bits=scalable`.

blocks.text:
These requirements come from the [Ubuntu CPU baseline](https://ubuntu.com/project/docs/how-ubuntu-is-made/concepts/supported-architectures/) and
[RISC-V QEMU requirements](https://ubuntu.com/hardware/docs/boards/how-to/ubuntu_supported/qemu-riscv/).
Older QEMU versions may fail before the container shell or Python starts.
Run this from the repository root.
./docker/run.sh all

`all` builds the image for each environment, captures raw C wrapper and shared C ABI results, and compares them with Intel. `verify` also runs CMake/CTest in each environment and Python, browser, sanitizer, and cross-build checks in the host-CPU container. The default output directory is artifacts/docker/.
./docker/run.sh all artifacts/docker/run-001

The comparison checks return values and memory output according to the case contract. A bit_exact contract also requires matching NaN signs and payloads and signed zero. A result that violates the contract remains an unresolved port mismatch even when CPU-specific behavior explains the difference. Mismatches return exit code 1; build and execution failures are recorded separately as errors.

sections.title: Compare a larger set of boundary inputs

blocks.text:
EQUILANE_PROFILE=adversarial ./docker/run.sh all artifacts/adversarial
EQUILANE_PROFILE=adversarial ./docker/run.sh verify artifacts/adversarial-verified

The adversarial input profile searches for mistakes in Intel Intrinsics ports. By default it generates 512 inputs for each of 253 operations and all 256 possible inputs for _mm_set1_epi8, for a total of 129,792 inputs per target. This is about 63.9 times the 2,032-input smoke run. The 762 raw-wrapper samples remain a separate execution path.

Inputs cover integer minima and maxima, saturation and conversion boundaries, bit and lane permutations, ±0, subnormals, infinity, NaN signs and payloads, rounding boundaries, every immediate declared by the case, shift-width boundaries, and valid memory offsets with guards and exact-fit buffers. The generator does not extend the contract to undeclared immediates, alignments, or rounding modes.
EQUILANE_PROFILE=adversarial EQUILANE_COUNT_PER_CASE=2048 ./docker/run.sh all artifacts/adversarial-large

Increasing the count includes remaining structured inputs before adding seeded raw-bit inputs. _mm_set1_epi8 is limited to 256 inputs regardless of the requested count. All CPUs use the same test-vectors.jsonl so the comparison conditions stay identical.

rows: SHA-256 of the actual input file, unique input counts per case, counts per test category, missing boundary bits, immediates, and memory offsets
Every mismatch and non-comparable result found while checking the full input set
Individual replay bundles; adversarial retains the first 128 by default
Full counts per target and links to reports; detailed HTML displays the first 128 entries by default

blocks.text: Input coverage describes which inputs were generated, not the C execution success rate or agreement with Intel. A 512-input run is not treated as exhaustive; uncovered scenarios are explicit in the coverage JSON. Limiting detailed display to 128 entries does not skip comparison or counting of any input.

sections.title: Capture targets individually and compare again

blocks.text:
./docker/run.sh intel
./docker/run.sh openpower
./docker/run.sh arm
./docker/run.sh riscv
./docker/run.sh compare

Selecting one target captures its output. `compare` compares saved Intel output with each target.
Use the same output directory for captures that belong to one comparison.
Environment variables control the following settings.

rows: Set to `0` to use existing images
CPU configuration for the RISC-V emulator
Parallelism for native workers and builds
Input profile for the shared C ABI; choose adversarial for a larger boundary-input set
Input count per shared C ABI case, capped at the number of unique inputs in a finite input domain

blocks.text: After building the images once, recapture results without rebuilding unchanged code:
EQUILANE_BUILD=0 ./docker/run.sh all artifacts/docker/repeat

On Docker hosts other than RISC-V, all / verify / wrappers automatically capture VLEN 256 as well as VLEN 128. A run on a RISC-V host cannot change the physical CPU VLEN through configuration. Use EQUILANE_RISCV_CPU to change the emulator baseline.
EQUILANE_RISCV_CPU=rva23s64,vlen=256 ./docker/run.sh all artifacts/docker/vlen256

QEMU selects its CPU through `QEMU_CPU`. The [QEMU implementation](https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/master/linux-user/main.c) confirms that this variable corresponds to `-cpu`.
This configures QEMU running under Docker; it does not add features to a physical CPU.

The raw-wrapper comparison has 254 operations × 3 inputs, or 762 samples per target. The shared C ABI comparison defaults to the smoke profile with 8 inputs per case, or 2,032 inputs. Raw-wrapper results are saved under intel/, openpower/, arm/, and riscv/; shared C ABI results are saved under native/<role>/.

rows: Capture metadata, including compiler, execution type, and image
Generated calling code, executable, and object files
Comparison results and differences from Intel

blocks.text:
Execution type is recorded as `docker-native` or `docker-emulated` using the Docker daemon CPU.
The daemon CPU is used even when it differs from the Mac running the Docker client.
An emulated result is an observation of that QEMU implementation. Check each run artifact for completion, match counts, and mismatch counts.

The initial baseline on 2026-11-10 captured all 762 samples for all four targets.
There were 25 differences from Intel on OpenPOWER, 24 on ARM64, and 23 on RISC-V64 (VLEN 128); the comparison command returned exit code 1.
The environment and counts are recorded in [Native status](../documentation/native-status.json).

The raw-wrapper runner calls the official C wrappers directly and runs three nearest-even inputs per operation. The separate run-native path decodes canonical inputs through the shared C ABI and implements contract-requested rounding and FP exception observation, pointer-buffer output, dynamic-symbol auditing, and process isolation. Neither path uses the Python model as its expected result. Shared ABI artifacts use the format accepted by compare-results, failure bundles, and verify-replay.
docker compose up --build studio

Open [localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765).
Studio runs in a host-CPU container and saves generated reports under `artifacts/studio/`.
Stop it with `Ctrl+C`; use the same command to restart it.

Studio `check` uses the existing Python development fixture.
To run the CLI in the same image, select a built target image and output directory.

mkdir -p artifacts/docker/fixture
docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 \
  --mount type=bind,src="$(pwd)/artifacts/docker/fixture",dst=/artifacts \
  equilane/ubuntu26.04:arm \
  equilane check --target all --output /artifacts/check --showcase-report

This example uses the ARM64 image. For another CPU, select matching platform and image tags.
Independent model checks in `check --quality` have known mismatches, which remain test failures in Docker.
See the [mismatch report](../MISMATCH_REPORT.md) and [native implementation scope](../documentation/native-status.json).

verification.evidence_method: Retained native Docker executions plus latest-source quality and separately refreshed, reauthenticated reports; see native-contract.json.

purpose: Verify that Intel Intrinsics have been ported correctly to other CPUs.
